The only clock is `clk`; the inputs are `d` (8 bits) and `reset` (1 bit); the output is `q` (8 bits). The phrase "synchronous reset" is the central constraint: reset is sampled at the rising edge like any other input, and it affects `q` only through that edge. There is no asynchronous clear, no partial-byte reset, and no per-bit masking. When `reset` is high at a sampled rising edge, all eight flip-flops are set to zero together; when `reset` is low at that edge, each flip-flop loads its corresponding bit of `d`. Thus the post-edge value is exactly `0x00` under reset, otherwise exactly the 8-bit `d` value present at that edge.

A mid-row assertion of `reset` is therefore not an immediate clear; it only prepares the next rising edge to force zero. A mid-row change of `d` likewise does not alter the current `q`; it is carried forward to the next sampled edge.

The checker should also avoid assuming any particular power-up value of `q` before the first sampled rising edge. The specification defines no asynchronous power-up state, so the pre-first-edge `q` is unspecified or seed-dependent. Strict comparisons should begin from the first post-edge sample, while still honoring any reset value carried into that first edge. After a sampled edge with `reset = 1`, all eight bits are known to be zero; subsequent edges with `reset = 0` load `d`.
